thread:
alex: Deploybot queued a CONFIG-ONLY change for tonight's window (starts 17:15 UTC). Params: default_batch_window_ms 25 -> 15, tenant_rate_cap 100 -> 80, routing_policy: prefer-dense-gpu, canary_traffic=5%, model_pin: redwood-3b@v20260322-canary. Change id cfg-20260322-17:15. Looking for ops + oncall ack and a rollback trigger.

deploy-bot: Change cfg-20260322-17:15 queued. Preflight checks: rollout plan ok, low-risk, safety gates enabled. Deploybot will auto-abort if error_rate > 0.5% or p99 latency delta > +80ms.

mike: ack. i'll watch p99 and queue alerts to #eng-oncall.

sophia: i'll enable additional perf traces. if kv-cache pressure rises, we rollback. advise adding temporary kvcache_bypass for long tails?

alex: good call. not in this change; prefer to observe first. rollback cmd below if needed: ```/rollback cfg-20260322-17:15 --reason="latency spike"```

jordan: canary traffic is 5% across geo, correct?

alex: yes. canary is per-tenant sampling 5% for 30m then evaluate.

deploy-bot: Canary started -> 5% traffic. Monitoring channels: #eng-releases for ops, #prod-metrics for dashboards.

mike: seeing small p95 bump +8ms, p99 stable. continuing to monitor. :eyes: 

sophia: KV cache miss rate up 2.1% on canary hosts, expected. if it exceeds 4% for 2 consecutive 5m windows we'll rollback.

alex: agreed. who will press rollback if that happens?

mike: i'll do it. I have permissions. i will post a short note with reason.

deploy-bot: Canary progressed to 20% after manual approval. Change now at 20% traffic. Auto-rollback still enabled.

jordan: false positive alert fired earlier, ignore. system noise.

mike: p99 spiked to +95ms on one AZ at 17:36 -> rolling back canary to 0% now.

deploy-bot: Rollback executed by mike at 1728004369. Change cfg-20260322-17:15 reverted. Root cause: uneven batching pressure on dense-gpu nodes causing KV cache thrash.

alex: thanks mike. postmortem notes: revert, add gradual batch_slope config, and a follow-up staged test with a microbatch of 10 tokens.

sophia: I'll collect traces and attach to the ticket. filing follow-up: REDW-987 - 'batch window tuning + kvcache mitigation'.

mike: all good. closing the change. leaving notes in release log.
